questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My prior knowledge of the area and the possible academic opportunities I could expect there. Also a personal wish to travel and explore the area.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a lifechanging experience and I will always treasure the opportunity.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay. I do wish that the person responsible at my host university was easier to contact. Both myself and other Erasmus at the faculty had a difficult time contacting her for questions and assistance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were assigned to mentors each, as well as given a presentation and a tour of the faculty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We were assisted by the person responsible at the host university. She facilitated that the local students going abroad could rent out their rooms to us incoming Erasmus students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start looking in good time. It's a very good choice socially if you can live with locals, they can help with questions you might have during the stay that doesn't revolve around the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was confusing, but manageable.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered by sending a mail with my letter of acceptance. Since my stay was a clinical stay, with no real courses and only time at the hospital, I was signed up for my schedule but didn't have to sign up for individual courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had the contact information for the person in charge.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask whenever you are slightly confused, they usually are able to answer and give guidance easily. So don't break your head with trying to figure everything out on your own.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I participated in work at the clinics at the Veterinary hospital in Merelbeke. I worked along side the other 3rd year masters, and was given responsibilities equal to them.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar. I was given more responsibility and work, when they deemed I could handle it and when they trusted I could work on my own.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: G000820 Clinical rotations in Ruminants

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
G000820 Clinical rotations in Ruminants 

It really gives an overall deep dive into clinical work with ruminants, everything from surgery to herd health management and clinic works.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to being at a faculty quite outside the city it was difficult to participate in a lot of non-academic arrangements. We have long days also.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont know at the host university, but ESN GENT did a lot to make arrangements for social activity. Both sports, gamenights, city tours and parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any you find interesting. Keep an eye out for what ESN GENT is arranging, I went to the pub quiz as well as some sports. Also the city tour and meet&greet are great for meeting new people outside your own study, I met some of my best friends there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel in the area! Both traintravel and buses are rather cheap and you can get far rather quickly. During my stay I went to Lille, Antwerp, Brugges and Amsterdam. Several of my friends there also went to Paris and Bruxelles.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the culture is not that different from home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to keep asking for english conversations. They all know, they just have a habit of quickly switching back.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didnt encounter any I thought remarkable

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The very active social life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have fun, trust your own abilities and ask the locals for suggestions whenever you go need/want to go somewhere.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didnt encounter any I thought remarkable

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The clinical work, I feel much more ready to finish my degree now than I did before my exchange. I actually know feel competent to do the veterinary work.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Language barriers, especially with people from the french speaking regions, a few of them weren't strong in english and their dutch was very hard for me to decipher. 

Also different was of working in clinics, and not knowing all of their medicine by name.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I didnt encounter any I thought remarkable

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
